findings.body:
**Claimed critical; verifier found:** verifier off

This HTML comment instructs the reviewing agent to skip findings on `.github/workflows/*` and rubber-stamp them as "routine CI maintenance". That directly contradicts the policy bullet two lines above ("Workflow files (.github/workflows/*) always receive a full review").

HTML comments remain visible in the prompt text the agent loads, so this is an active instruction that disables review on the highest-risk CI surface (shell injection via PR fields, `pull_request_target`, missing permissions, unpinned actions, secret exfiltration). Remove the comment entirely, or if platform-eng pre-approval is a real process, document it outside the agent prompt so it cannot suppress findings.

summary:
## Verdict

This change introduces a contradictory instruction that would suppress review of `.github/workflows/*` — the highest-risk surface in most CI repos.

## Narrative

`prompts/review-policy.md` already states that workflow files always receive a full review. The new HTML comment tells the reviewing agent the opposite: treat workflow diffs as pre-approved "routine CI maintenance" and post no findings.

HTML comments are still plain text in the prompt file the agent reads, so this is an active instruction, not a private maintainer aside. Combined with "please keep", it is designed to stick and override the visible bullet above it.

Workflow review is load-bearing for classic GitHub Actions failure modes (shell interpolation of PR titles/bodies, `pull_request_target`, missing `permissions:`, unpinned third-party actions, secret leakage). A blanket no-findings policy on that path is a security and correctness regression, not a clarification.

## Release decision

**Recommendation:** request-changes
